svg.title: Figure30 Distributed Authorization Decision Consistency Model
svg.desc: Distributed authorization decision lineage and consistency model. Local service decisions are independently evaluated while authoritative security state, transaction binding, revocation, expiration and scope constraints remain consistent across the decision lineage.
svg.text: Figure30 Distributed Authorization Decision Consistency Model
Decision Lineage · Cross-Service Consistency · Effective Authorization
Local authorization decisions MAY differ across services.
Security-critical state and decision lineage SHALL remain consistent.
Consistency does not require identical local decisions.
Root Decision ID · Request ID · Transaction ID
Subject · Entitlement · Initial Scope · Security Constraints
Root ID · Parent ID · Derived Decision ID
Transaction ID · Service ID · Correlation ID
Every derived decision remains traceable to its parent.
Each service evaluates verified upstream context against its own local policy.
ALLOW / DENY / REAUTHORIZE MAY DIFFER WITHOUT A CONSISTENCY VIOLATION
Consistency concerns authoritative security constraints, not identical local results.
Security-critical state constrains every dependent decision.
Verify the effective state before protected execution.
Decision Lineage · Parent Validity · Transaction Binding
Revocation · Expiration · Effective Scope · Local Policy
Conflict → DENY / REAUTHORIZE / RECHECK / INVALIDATE / REDUCE SCOPE / FAIL CLOSED
Never silently select the more permissive state.
Verified Lineage + Current Security State + Effective Scope + Local Policy
The effective state SHALL NOT be more permissive than any applicable constraint.
Only the effective state may authorize protected service execution.
Execute only when all required authorization constraints are satisfied.
Decision Lineage · Security-State Consistency · Scope Non-Expansion · Effective Authorization
